rationale: No public block matches this shape in any of the four collections (verified absent). `columns` is a close structural host (0.75) but is a generic layout primitive: authors get free-form cells with no guidance that cell 1 must be the image, and loading it with 2 layout + 4 brand background variants (including the gradient and its white-text coupling) turns a shared primitive into a brand component. A dedicated block gives named fields and makes the gradient own its own text colour in CSS — which is the specific authoring smell the source exhibits (white text hand-applied per element via span.text__color--primary-white).
source_contract: wrapper carries background class (e.g. color-grad-red-plum-diag); __content carries layout class (image-left|image-right); __card holds h2 + rich description (p, br, sup, ul) + optional a.primary-button.
alternative: EXTEND `columns` with image-left/image-right + background variants. Cheaper (no new block, exact 50/50 and mobile stacking already work) but weaker author model and pollutes a shared primitive.

component: product-card grid (4 cards on stone band)
rationale: The blocking gap is structural, not cosmetic: cards.js gives a picture-only cell .cards-card-image and collapses EVERY other cell into .cards-card-body, so there is no hook for a discrete eyebrow. The source card carries an inline --accent-color custom property, a distinct eyebrow, an H4, a <sup>-bearing description, and 1..n aria-labelled forward links. The `card` model is image + richtext only, so all of that would be smuggled into one richtext blob and targeted with fragile nth-child CSS. Extending the shared `cards` model would also push product-specific fields onto every card author site-wide.
alternative: EXTEND `cards` with a decorate() extension for the eyebrow hook plus a per-card colour token. Avoids a new block but mutates a shared model.
